userStories.title: Make the provenance guard survive squash-merge and shallow clones (R4-m1)
userStories.description: As the tool owner, I want the ml test suite to stay green on main after this branch is squash-merged. (CODE_REVIEW_R4 R4-m1) Evidence: main has 0 merge commits (PRs land as single-parent squash commits), so the recorded generating sha 6f56cf8 can never be an ancestor of main HEAD — test_committed_evidence_git_sha_is_ancestor_of_head (tests/test_committed_model_evidence.py) fails 14 parametrized cases permanently after merge (reproduced by simulating the squash with git commit-tree). A 'git clone --depth 1' also hard-fails: 'git merge-base --is-ancestor' exits 128 ('Not a valid commit name') and _require_git_checkout only skips when git is missing or cwd is not a work tree, so exit 128 is asserted as non-ancestry.
acceptanceCriteria: Read ml/SPEC.md AND the R4-m1 finding in ml/CODE_REVIEW_R4.md in full before starting

The provenance guard no longer requires the manifest sha to be an ancestor of the CURRENT HEAD; replace with a check that survives squash-merge — e.g. every evidence manifest's git_sha equals the sha recorded in a single committed evidence-pass file (ml/artifacts/EVIDENCE_PASS.json or equivalent) that US-406 rewrites, AND all manifests share that one sha (keep test_evidence_pass_uses_one_shared_git_sha), AND git_dirty is false — the R2-M2/R3-M2 staleness class stays detectable because a regenerated-elsewhere artifact would carry a sha that differs from the pass file

Where git is consulted at all, exit code 128 / missing object results in pytest.skip with a clear reason, never an assertion failure; verified in a 'git clone --depth 1' of the branch under /tmp (full suite: 0 failures)
Verified in a simulated squash checkout under /tmp (git commit-tree HEAD^{tree} -p $(git merge-base origin/main HEAD)): the evidence tests pass, not fail
A test proves the guard still catches staleness: in a /tmp copy, stamp one manifest with a different well-formed sha and confirm a named test fails

userStories.title: Close the two remaining session-clobber paths (R4-m2)
userStories.description: As the tool owner drafting in two leagues on the same night, I want NO code path to silently overwrite a session log. (CODE_REVIEW_R4 R4-m2) US-302's refusal lives only in the new-session branch of cli/draft.py (~line 810). Two sibling paths still clobber, both reproduced live: (a) 'oracle draft --resume A.json --session B.json' with an existing, different B.json — the --resume branch (~line 799) sets session_path = session or resume and _run_loop's pre-loop _autosave() writes A's contents over B (verified: 2-pick log -> 0 picks, no message); (b) the in-loop 'resume <path>' command replaces the session object and immediately autosaves it to the ORIGINAL launch session_path, destroying the launch log (verified: league1.json ended up holding league2's picks and slot).
acceptanceCriteria: Read ml/SPEC.md AND the R4-m2 finding in ml/CODE_REVIEW_R4.md in full before starting

'--resume A --session B' refuses with a clear message when B exists and is not the same file as A (resuming A in place, i.e. B omitted or B == A, keeps working); the round-4 reproduction (existing 2-pick B) is the regression test and B must be byte-identical afterwards

The in-loop 'resume <path>' command never writes the resumed session over the launch log: either the autosave target switches to the resumed path (announced to the user) or the command refuses when the launch log holds picks that differ; the round-4 reproduction (league1.json 2 picks, resume league2.json, quit) is the regression test and league1.json must be unchanged
README's draft-assistant section documents the resume semantics chosen

userStories.title: Override count-guard consistency: corrected_name-aware counting and team-side enforcement (R4-m5, R4-m4)
userStories.description: As the tool owner, I want the expected_matches guard to count exactly what the override consumes. (CODE_REVIEW_R4 R4-m5, R4-m4) Evidence: _validate_player_override_match_counts (ingest/entity_match.py ~210-228) counts skater rows by normalize_name(raw player_or_team_name), but build_league_draft_picks (~679-683) applies overrides via match_skater(corrected_name or raw) — verified: setting corrected_name='Connor McDavid' on the 2024 R3_4 row silently bypasses the Draisaitl override while the guard still passes (corrected_name is in real use: row 104 Makar -> Evan Bouchard). Separately, load_name_overrides (~196) parses expected_matches for the teams: section and binds it to _team_expected_matches, then drops it — NameOverrides has no team field, so a team override declaring a count would appear guarded and never be.

The count-guard keys on the exact name the override lookup consumes (corrected_name when present, else raw) — the round-4 bypass (corrected_name='Connor McDavid' on the 2024 McDavid row) now trips the guard with 'found 0'; the committed corpus still validates (McDavid expected 1 found 1) and levi's row still resolves to 8477934

userStories.title: Reporting and doc polish: live ESPN favorite flag, series-sim sample size, r3 goalie fold contract, manifest disclosures (R4-m6, R4-m7, R4-m8, info items)
userStories.description: As the tool owner, I want the last reporting inconsistencies gone. (CODE_REVIEW_R4 R4-m6, R4-m7, R4-m8 + info) Evidence: (R4-m6) espn_summary_to_rows (ingest/odds.py ~1800) selects the moneyline via the per-side favorite flag, then discards the side and sets favorite_side from the spread, defaulting to 'away' covered=True when the spread is missing/blank — the offline completion parser already returns unattributed in that case; (R4-m7) series_sim.py ~770 hard-codes 'With ~40 playoff series held out' while the same report and manifest say series_scored: 30; (R4-m8) _apply_combined_valuation (projection_artifact.py ~362) folds R4 into e_goalie_points only, so on artifacts/2026-r3/teams.csv the SPEC identity e_goalie_points == 2E[wins]+2E[shutouts] fails by up to 4.73 (COL) while holding to 1e-15 on r1/r2/r4, and README's teams column list never mentions the fold; info items: run manifests don't record generating CLI flags (r4 was built with --no-slot-strategies), fixtures reproduce to float-ULP not byte-identically across platforms (the one_step row 58.44 vs 58.31 Windows-vs-Linux divergence is the uncertain finding), the opponent membership evaluation silently drops 2025 R1 (no snake order in the sheet), and SPEC section 5 / PROVENANCE still describe the Kaggle/ESPN 2022-23..2025-26 favorite prices as usable although the pipeline correctly carries them covered=False.
acceptanceCriteria: Read ml/SPEC.md AND the R4-m6/R4-m7/R4-m8 findings and the info observations in ml/CODE_REVIEW_R4.md in full before starting

espn_summary_to_rows derives favorite_side from the per-side favorite flag it already reads; when neither flag nor a usable spread exists the row is unattributed/uncovered (mirroring parse_espn_completion); tested with the missing/None/blank spread and flag-vs-spread-disagreement payloads
The series-sim honesty note derives its sample size from counts.series_scored (no hard-coded '~40'); tested via the report renderer

The r3 combined fold is part of the column contract: either emit companion columns (e_wins_combined, e_shutout_wins_combined) so the goalie identity is recomputable from the table, or document in README's teams column list and the artifact cheatsheet header exactly which columns are R3-only vs combined; a test asserts the identity on r1/r2/r4 and the documented fold relation on r3

Run manifests record the generating CLI flags (e.g. slot_strategies on/off, rollouts) and a platform note (os/python/numpy versions) so a rebuild can be compared like-for-like; the reproducibility statement in README/SPEC says 'to float-ULP across platforms, byte-identical on the generating platform'

The opponent report discloses which events are excluded from membership evaluation and why (2025 R1: no snake order in the sheet); SPEC section 5 and odds-archive/PROVENANCE.md state that the Kaggle/ESPN favorite prices for 2022-23 onward are carried covered=False by the pipeline
Any report/manifest writer change here does NOT regenerate committed artifacts in this story — US-406 regenerates everything in one pass so the shared-sha guard holds
